mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a raw shell build-out and a second-generation remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: A shell build-out starts with an empty space consisting only of exterior walls, a concrete floor slab, and basic utility stubs, offering complete freedom to design your layout from scratch at a higher initial construction cost. A second-generation remodel alters a previously occupied office. Second-generation spaces offer significant cost savings if you can reuse existing restrooms, HVAC zones, lighting, or partition walls. However, second-generation projects may require selective demolition, code updates to older wiring or plumbing, and minor compromises on optimal floor-plan efficiency.
acceptedAnswer.description: A raw shell provides complete design flexibility from a blank slate, while a second-generation remodel repurposes existing structures, often lowering upfront construction costs.
